title: Circular Measure Module 7 Lesson 1: Tangents & Advanced Composite Capstones custom practice

parts.prompt: From an external point $P$, tangents touch a circle of radius $5\text{ cm}$ at points $A$ and $B$. Given that the distance from the centre $O$ to $P$ is $13\text{ cm}$, find the exact length of tangent $PA$.
From an external point $P$, tangents touch a circle of radius $3\text{ cm}$ at $A$ and $B$. Given that $OP = 6\text{ cm}$, find the exact central angle $\angle AOB$ in radians in terms of $\pi$.
Tangents from point $P$ touch a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$ at $A$ and $B$, with tangent length $PA = 8\text{ cm}$. Find the total area of the kite $OAPB$.
Tangents from point $P$ touch a circle of radius $6\text{ cm}$ at $A$ and $B$. Given that $\angle APB = \dfrac{\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$, find the exact length of the minor arc $AB$ in terms of $\pi$.

From point $P$, tangents touch a circle of radius $3\text{ cm}$ at $A$ and $B$, where $\angle AOB = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}\text{ radians}$ and $PA = PB = 3\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}$. Find the exact area bounded by $PA$, $PB$ and the minor arc $AB$ in the form $a\sqrt{3} - b\pi$, where $a$ and $b$ are integers.

A taut belt runs from point $P$ along two tangents $PA$ and $PB$ of length $10\text{ cm}$ each to a circle of radius $5\text{ cm}$, and wraps around the major arc $AB$. Given that the minor central angle is $\angle AOB = 1.2\text{ radians}$, find the total length of the belt in terms of $\pi$.
From point $P$, $OP=10$ cm to the centre of a circle of radius $6$ cm. Tangents touch at $A$ and $B$. Find $PA$ and the minor angle $\angle AOB$.
